title: IMUSA USA Granite Molcajete Spice Grinder 6-Inch, Gray
description:
About this item
MEASUREMENTS AND BENEFITS: With a 6 inche diameter, this Granite Molcajete is perfect for preparing small to medium sized batches of your favorite recipes, its size provides efficient grinding and mashing of spices, herbs, and more
DURABLE CONSTRUCTION: Crafted from durable granite with a natural finish, this mortar and pestle set is easy to clean, offers long lasting performance, and features a comfortable, curved pestle for easy use

reviews_5s:
Bought in 2018 Jan I still have it in 2025 and is perfect as it was. I use this every single day.This heavy duty mortor& pestle is ideal for crushing nuts etc...Love it, it is even larger than I assumedEasily crush your garlic, ginger and other spices. This grinder is sturdy and easy to use.Click to play video
The IMUSA USA Granite Molcajete Spice Grinder is a game-changer in my kitchen! Not only does it look rustic and authentic on my countertop, but it also crushes and grinds spices, herbs, and even guacamole ingredients like a pro.

The granite feels solid and durable, and the texture creates the perfect surface for blending flavors. Plus, using it makes me feel like a gourmet chef—there’s something so satisfying about grinding spices by hand.Highly recommend !A good size and rough at the bottom for easy grinding.This is a very strong bowl and very heavy. It crushes nuts, garlic ginger etc. Very handy when cooking.Works excellent!!This molcajete has a lot going for it. The great benefit is the surface of the mortar and pestle are rough which facilitates rapid grinding and mashing. Gets through seeds and herbs in a fraction of the time of the highly polished versions.
Requires a few extra seconds of cleaning but saves minuets of grinding.
Of course the price is exceptional as well.
Great bargain and wish I had bought one like it 40 years ago/I picked this up on a Lightning Deal and am very happy with the purchase. Traditional molcajetes are made with lava rock, which is much rougher than this granite one, but it is sturdy nonetheless. Because it is unpolished, there is much more friction that takes place when breaking down herbs, vegetables, spices, etc. If you are looking for something smoother, go for a polished material like marble, steel, or even granite. This is meant to be a rougher surface based on the dishes that are most likely to be prepared in/with it.

That aside, I did use some rice, salt, and a bit of water before my first use in an attempt to cure the surface of the bowl. I actually repeated the process 3 times before my first use to make sure that I had worn off any loose granite bits and dust from the manufacturing process. While a bit time consuming, I liken it to seasoning a cast iron pan. For those of you that use them, was your pan perfect when you first bought it? I would venture a guess of "no" and the same is true here. Time and use will make this molcajete smoother and a bit easier to use.

The biggest advantage is being able to use the bowl for serving once you are finished. Tip: I use a cork trivet underneath during operation to avoid slipping, surface scratching (the legs are very rough), and it helps with vibration absorption. Overall, I am happy to use this and keep it on display in my kitchen.
